name: Papua New Guinean panpipe and polyphonic singing
lineage: Papua New Guinean polyphonic vocal-and-panpipe traditions across the New Guinea Highlands (Eastern Highlands, Western Highlands, Chimbu, Enga regions), with each linguistic-cultural group preserving distinct multi-part vocal-or-instrumental polyphonic conventions. The Huli yodel-and-cyclic-clap, the Hagen courtship-chants, the Enga sandalu and tee public-ceremony chants, and the Chimbu collective-flute ensembles each represent distinct contributions to the broader New Guinea polyphonic-music register. Performance contexts span bridewealth-negotiation ceremonies, mourning-rituals, harvest-festivals, and (post-1975 independence) the National Cultural Commission and University of Papua New Guinea ethnomusicology archive preservation work. Distinguished from neighboring Melanesian musical traditions by New Guinea Highlands-specific polyphonic-density and dialect-specific intonation vocabularies.
